correctness.rationale: Exact cross-bifix-free binary length-10 code of size 17 forces all encoded proper overlaps to be multiples of ten and preserves every overlap and greedy merge. Independently reconstructed 252 distinct length-eight source windows and the 17 codewords, checked each of 251 prescribed merges against the maximum over all live ordered pairs, all 63,252 ordered distinct source/binary input overlaps, the Eulerian 259-symbol optimal superstring, and output 519. Distinct length-80 inputs with max proper overlap 70 have starting positions at least ten apart in any superstring, proving OPT >=80+251*10=2590 and attainable. Greedy length=5190 so ratio 519/259>2. The finite certificate is exhaustive for this explicit instance; it is not a universal greedy approximation theorem.

value.rationale: The common-length binary shortest-superstring greedy ratio is a natural quantitative benchmark. The full 252-string exact instance cuts binary length from 288 under the cited general 17-letter alphabet reduction to 80, with exact OPT and a reproducible legal adversarial greedy trace. It neither proves that length 80 is minimal nor that all tie-breakings fail. This small but material 3.6-fold reduction in binary benchmark size is useful in algorithm testing.

limitations: An earlier 17-word length-10 cross-bifix-free code or compiled binary superstring counterexample may independently contain the same 80-bit bound.
The result concerns worst legal tie-breaking for a single binary set, not an optimal minimal-bit threshold.
